what: The working vault handed to the agent at riskmandate.ai: who is being contacted, through which published route, what was said and what came back. Separate from the corpus vault on purpose — that one is a finished record of what somebody else published, this one is an append-only record of what we do about it.
why_private: The outreach vault holds who we are contacting and what we plan to say. That is ours until it is sent, and it was a mistake to publish a read key for it at v0.4.4. The vault was rekeyed on 2026-09-29 with `sgit vault move`: every object re-encrypted under a new key, pushed under a new identity, and the old vault hard-deleted from the server. The read key published between v0.4.4 and v0.5.3 now opens nothing — verified by cloning with it and recovering zero files.

revoked_read_keys.how: sgit vault move: every object re-encrypted under a new key, pushed under a new identity, old vault hard-deleted from the server
revoked_read_keys.verified: cloning with it recovers 0 files — 'no branch index and no named ref'
revoked_read_keys.why_it_is_recorded_here: So the gate can hunt it. A revoked key that nobody tracks creeps back into a generated file; llms-full.txt still had it after llms.txt was fixed, and only a check found that.

contents: README.md, protocol.md, brief.md, targets/ (one per organisation), actions/ (append-only, with its JSON schema), drafts/, state.json, evidence.md
no_read_key_is_published: Deliberately. This vault holds who is being contacted and what we plan to say, which is ours until it is sent.
